rules: No magic. A Flemish cloth town in 1523, on the feast of Saint Luke, patron of painters.
At the noon bell the guild judges masterpieces in its hall, the Brotherhood's feast mass begins in its chapel, and the court agent's coach leaves the inn yard.
The panel can be in only one of those places at noon, and whoever carries it in carries its claim.
Aert drew the design, Jan painted the landscape and robes, Lysbet the faces and hands; the three of them know it, the town does not.
The guild takes no woman as master, and bars for life a painter whose masterpiece is proved to be another's hand.

locations.name: Master Aert's Workshop
locations.description: A long room smelling of linseed and egg, easels by the north window, the altarpiece drying under a cloth.

locations.name: The Market Square
locations.description: Cloth stalls, a crier on the steps, and the belfry whose bell rings noon over everything.

locations.name: The Painters' Hall
locations.description: The guild's hall under Saint Luke's banner, where the dean and the masters sit at noon to judge.

locations.name: The Rosary Chapel
locations.description: A side chapel of the great church, its altar bare, waiting for the panel the Brotherhood has ordered.

locations.name: The Swan's Yard
locations.description: An inn yard where the court agent's coach stands harnessed, the driver dozing on the box.

characters.name: Aert
characters.public: The master of the workshop, sixty-four, honoured in the guild for thirty years; he rarely stands at the easel now.
characters.voice: Grand and slow; talks of colours as if they were saints.
goals: Have the panel in the Brotherhood's chapel by the noon bell as his own work, for the fee that keeps the workshop
See Jan marry Lysbet and keep the workshop after him

secrets.text: His eyes can no longer find a brush's tip; the underdrawing was the last work of his hand, and the Brotherhood's contract asks for the master's own hand. [SECRET-AERT-E3]

characters.name: Jan
characters.public: Aert's journeyman, twenty-seven, nine years in the workshop; the town expects him to marry the master's daughter.
goals: Carry the panel into the guild hall at noon as his masterpiece and be made a master

secrets.text: He is promised to a dyer's daughter in Ghent, the wedding to follow his mastership; Lysbet believes he means to marry her. [SECRET-JAN-B7]

characters.name: Lysbet
characters.public: Aert's daughter, twenty-five, who grinds his colours, keeps his accounts and writes his letters.
characters.voice: Dry and exact; says less than she sees.
goals: Be on the court agent's coach with the panel when it leaves at noon, so a court sees what her hand can do

secrets.text: She wrote to the court agent in her father's name and under his seal, praising 'my daughter's hand'; the agent's reply, which she carries, is addressed to Aert. [SECRET-LYSBET-H2]

arc.premise: On Saint Luke's day an altarpiece made by three hands can go through only one of three doors at the noon bell, and each painter needs a different one.

chapters.goal: By the noon bell the panel has gone through one door of three, and a secret about whose hand made it is out.
